claims.text: Controlled isothermal annealing causes thermally activated Mg diffusion out of a metastable solid solution.
Mg diffusion induces local phase separation and nucleation of intermetallic compounds.
The morphology and distribution of intermetallics control the evolution of a passivating oxide layer.
Intermetallic-mediated oxide-layer evolution controls retention or loss of both corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Rapid consolidation by methods such as ball milling and spark plasma sintering can produce the proposed homogeneous, metastable solid-solution initial state.
The alloy should be annealed at incremental temperatures such as 150, 200, and 250 °C under an inert atmosphere.
Post-anneal performance should be assessed in 0.1 M NaCl and at oxidation temperatures of 400–600 °C.
Local Mg segregation leads to heterogeneous intermetallic nucleation at grain boundaries and within grain interiors.
Ti2Zn and Mg21Zn25 are relevant example intermetallic phases in an Mg-containing Mg-Ti-Zn alloy.
A fine, uniformly distributed intermetallic network can promote or stabilize a protective passivating surface film.
Coarse intermetallic aggregates disrupt oxide continuity and facilitate corrosion.
Coarse intermetallic aggregates disrupt oxide continuity and accelerate high-temperature oxidation.
Annealing at 200–250 °C will produce a fine, uniformly distributed intermetallic network.
The intermediately annealed alloy will have better corrosion resistance than the initial metastable state or states with coarse intermetallics.
The intermediately annealed alloy will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than the initial metastable state or states with coarse intermetallics.
Near room temperature, Mg diffusion and associated transformation are minimal.
Temperatures up to 600 °C define the relevant high-temperature oxidation service regime for the proposed alloy.

The proposed mechanism is falsified if annealing produces no correlation between Mg segregation or intermetallic nucleation and passivation integrity, or if the predicted resistance improvement relative to the initial state is absent.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as produced by ball milling and spark plasma sintering, but elsewhere the same comparator is called 'as-quenched.' Quenching is not specified and is not equivalent to the stated powder-processing and sintering route.
